note: Advanced singing made musical: a fast run and an octave tune to open the range, then guide tones and a line of the singer's own over a ii-V-I the band plays, read from a staff. The why says what makes guide tones work (each one moves a step or stays), the guide-tone staff shows only those four notes, labelled by degree as the text names them, and the same changes come back in F with the guide tones ringed among the whole scale. The run's range is stated and each block says what to sing on.

exercise.title: Guide tones over ii-V-I, then your own line
exercise.why: The 3rd and the 7th are the notes that tell one chord from the next, and through a ii-V-I each of them moves by a step or stays where it is, so a line made of them lets you hear every change.

cells.text: Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run goes from La below Do up to the high Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it lightly on "ah", and move to "oo" when a pass feels tight.

Press Play below to hear a tune that opens with a leap of an octave. Sing along on "oo" and check where your line lands after the leap. Once it lands without a slide, sing the tune first and press Play to check.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the band. On "ah", sing one long note per chord: {{4}} over Dm7, {{4}} again over G7, then {{3}} over Cmaj7. Then the other line: {{1}} over Dm7, {{7}} over G7, {{7}} again over Cmaj7. Listen for the bar where your note stays and the chord changes under it.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the same changes in F: Gm7, C7, Fmaj7. Make up your own line on any vowel, and start each chord on one of its ringed notes: {{4}} or {{1}} over Gm7, {{7}} or {{4}} over C7, {{3}} or {{7}} over Fmaj7. Leave space between phrases.
